tools/checks/work-item-report.mjs 13/13. The report classifies every scheduled action (work_items — the invoices and reports §9-4 names) into six mutually exclusive buckets: overdue, due today, upcoming, unscheduled, done, cancelled. Each tile is asserted against an independent SQL count and the six must sum to the row count; the page states that reconciliation itself and says so when it breaks. Counting decisions, each tested: a cancelled item whose due date has passed is counted as cancelled and NOT as overdue, so the late-work number is not inflated (mutating the bucket to include cancelled rows makes the sum 15 against a total of 14 and drops the suite to 8/13); `unscheduled` reads 0 because work_items.due_date is NOT NULL and exists so the reconciliation still holds if that is ever relaxed. Completing an invoice through the real endpoint moves it between tiles. Kind filter, due-date range, sorting (with the sort column whitelisted — an injected column falls back rather than reaching SQL) and pagination all recomputed and re-reconciled. Amounts are gated on invoices.view; a viewer gets 403. §9-3's «مسئول» filter — the one project filter that was missing — is covered here too. Also fixed while writing this: ContractReportController eager-loaded `customer:id,legal_name,…`, and legal_name is not a column on customers (the legal name is company_name); displayName() branches on `type`, which was not selected either, so every legal customer rendered as «مشتری بدون نام» on a report marked VERIFIED. The traceability summary previously read "invoice PDF pending mPDF slice", which misstated the requirement: §12-9 asks for the invoice number, amount, issue date AND the invoice file to be recorded after sending. It is not a PDF-generation requirement — §9-7 names four PDFs (contract, project dossier, access information, payslip) and an invoice is not among them. Three of the four are implemented: POST /work-items/{id}/complete requires invoice_number and invoice_amount for an invoice item, validates the amount through Money::parse rather than silently storing 0, and stores invoice_issue_date. The fourth is not: work_items.document_attachment_id is fillable but nothing in app/ ever writes it, because recording a file needs the upload subsystem (REQ-10.06), which is not built. Marked PARTIAL rather than NOT_IMPLEMENTED because the previous status understated what works, and rather than VERIFIED because the file half genuinely does not.
REQ-14.01: tools/checks/phase4-integration.mjs 25/25 walks the nine integration chains end to end over HTTP with the resulting database state asserted at each link: A customer→contract→template→finalisation→PDF→project (the template is attached at finalisation, not at creation — StoreContractRequest has no template_id rule and the body is snapshotted by ContractFinalizer, so an unfinalised contract returns 409 by design); B project→expert→required accesses→finalisation gate, refused while accesses are missing and accepted once the three blocking kinds exist; C settings→validation→persistence→consumption, an invalid threshold refused with the stored value unchanged; D threshold→dashboard warning→contract report, the near-expiry tile matching independent SQL at both a 1-day and a 30-day window; E employee→assignment→workload report→payroll, one payslip per active employee; F keyword→SEO project→website address→search; G note→dashboard→completion→activity history; H global search→navigation→record authorization; I backup→integrity→restore→reconciliation, driving the real vira:backup and vira:restore commands and comparing every table's row count after the round trip (audit_logs may grow by one because the restore records itself). Three real defects came out of it. vira:restore prompts "Proceed?" and, with stdin closed, aborts while still exiting 0 — an unattended restore therefore needs --no-interaction, and a check that only read the exit code would have called a restore that wrote nothing a success. The dashboard had no notes panel at all, although §8 puts free notes on the dashboard and §2 asks for tasks near their due date; open notes are now listed there. And the dashboard's closing line still claimed the project, credentials, personnel, payroll and report modules "will be enabled in the next phase", which has not been true for several releases; it is removed.
